clusters.rule: Spell the Airflow concept and its Python class as `Dag`/`Dags` in prose - user-facing docs, newsfragments, release notes, config.yml descriptions, docstrings and test names - reserving all-caps `DAG` for code identifiers and quoted strings.
clusters.trigger: Prose in a newsfragment, release note, config.yml description, docstring or test name uses all-caps DAG/DAGs for the concept or the Python class, outside backticks or a code identifier.
clusters.rationale: Airflow 3 renamed the class to Dag and reviewers hold that spelling in prose; all-caps DAG now reads as the literal identifier, so mixing the two makes the docs look like they describe two different things.

clusters.rule: Read boolean Airflow configuration options with conf.getboolean(), never conf.get() or conf.has_option, and never pass a fallback that contradicts the option's declared default in config.yml.
clusters.trigger: conf.get(section, key, fallback=...) or conf.has_option(section, key) is used for a key that is a boolean elsewhere, or conf.getboolean(..., fallback=False) is used for a key whose config.yml default is True.
clusters.rationale: config.yml is the single source of truth for an option's type and default; reading a boolean through conf.get yields the raw string, and a contradicting fallback silently overrides the documented default.

clusters.rule: Reject an invalid query-parameter value with HTTP 400 instead of silently falling back to it: an unparseable cursor token and an empty regex pattern must both raise rather than reach the query.
clusters.trigger: An except block in _coerce_value or cursor-parsing code returns the original value rather than raising, or a regex query parameter such as partition_key_pattern is validated against None only and not against the empty string.
clusters.rationale: A silent fallback turns a client mistake into a wrong result set - a raw cursor value, or regexp_match on an empty pattern matching everything - so the API has to tell the caller the parameter was bad.

clusters.rule: Compare enum-typed values as Enum members: use the provider's or Airflow's Enum rather than raw string literals, and do not reach for .value before the comparison.
clusters.trigger: A comparison such as `if status != '<state_string>'` where a corresponding Enum already exists in the provider, or `DagRunType.<member>.value not in <collection>` where the collection holds enum members.
clusters.rationale: Enums exist so state comparisons survive renames and typos; degrading them to strings at the comparison site defeats that and hides the mismatch until runtime.

clusters.rule: Do not add or keep public surface that nothing consumes: a parameter, field or property must have a real consumer in the repository and a real effect; if it is unimplemented or no longer used, remove it from the signature and docstring, or make supplying it warn or raise.
clusters.trigger: A field is added to an execution-API datamodel with no worker-side reader, a property is added to a core base class such as CronMixin with no in-core reference site, an __init__ stores self.param that no method reads, or a parameter is dropped from a DagBag implementation body but kept in the signature or docstring.
clusters.rationale: Every exported name is a compatibility promise Airflow then has to keep; a parameter that is silently ignored or a field nobody reads is a promise with no behaviour behind it, and users only find the gap after depending on it.

clusters.rule: Do not commit the caller's shared session from inside a method that participates in a larger transaction: use session.flush(), or open an independent session with create_session(scoped=False) when the row must be visible before the caller commits.
clusters.trigger: session.commit() appears inside register_asset_change, assets/manager.py or another method invoked as part of a multi-model task-completion transaction, instead of session.flush() or a separate create_session(scoped=False) block.
clusters.rationale: Committing the shared session ends a transaction the caller still owns, so a later failure can no longer roll the whole unit of work back; a visibility requirement is met with a second session, not by cutting the caller's transaction short.

clusters.rule: A broad `except Exception` must not swallow or re-wrap an exception that is deliberately raised to propagate: re-raise the specific type before the generic handler, and when introducing such an exception, update every enclosing fall-through loop to let it through in the same change.
clusters.trigger: An except Exception block in dag_processing/ wraps a sentinel such as CallbackBundleUnavailable, a `raise AirflowException(...)` sits inside a try whose downstream `except Exception as e` re-wraps it, or a secrets backend is made to raise PermissionError without changing the `except Exception: continue` backend-iteration loops in execution_time/context.py and models/connection.py.
clusters.rationale: These handlers exist to tolerate incidental failures; when they also catch the exception a caller was meant to see, the deliberate signal disappears and the system quietly does the wrong thing - a denied secret simply falls through to the next backend.

clusters.rule: Put behaviour that every concrete subclass needs in the shared base class or mixin - BaseExecutor, BaseCoordinator, BaseNotifier - rather than re-implementing it, or repeating the version guard, in each concrete implementation.
clusters.trigger: A new workload-handling method or branch is added to several concrete executor files with no base-class implementation, a new per-language coordinator re-implements socket server startup or accept helpers, or an `if AIRFLOW_V_x_y_PLUS:` guard is added inside a concrete Notifier.
clusters.rationale: Airflow's concrete executors, coordinators and notifiers live across providers and out-of-tree code Airflow does not control; anything the base class can do for them is a change every one of those implementations is spared.

clusters.rule: Log a caught exception with its full exception information - self.log.exception(...) or exc_info=True as a structlog keyword - rather than suppressing it silently or recording only str(exc).
clusters.trigger: `with suppress(Exception):` is introduced around an await in triggerer_job_runner.py, or a log.debug/log.warning call under task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/coordinators/ passes error=str(exc) instead of exc_info=True.
clusters.rationale: Cleanup and coordinator paths are exactly where failures are invisible; without the traceback there is nothing to debug from, and a bare suppress removes even the fact that something failed.

clusters.rule: Do not write an inline try/except ImportError compatibility shim where a central layer already handles the import - airflow.utils.sqlalchemy for SQLAlchemy 1.4/2.0 differences, airflow.providers.common.compat for provider redirects - or where the import cannot fail in the supported version.
clusters.trigger: A model file adds a try/except ImportError block to shim mapped_column or Mapped from sqlalchemy.orm, or a core test or provider module adds a `try: from airflow.X import Y / except ImportError:` block for a symbol the current core exports or common.compat already redirects.
clusters.rationale: Compat shims are load-bearing and have to be retired deliberately; scattering redundant copies through individual files hides which ones still matter and leaves dead branches nobody can safely delete.

clusters.rule: Distinguish absence from a legitimate falsy value: test with `is not None` in Python and an explicit undefined/null check in TypeScript, and do not collapse None into an empty container with `param or []`, wherever 0, False, an empty string or an empty collection carry meaning.
clusters.trigger: `if bundle_version:`, `Boolean(value)` or `if (value)` is used as a presence check on a field whose valid domain includes falsy values (a map_index of 0, a falsy XCom value), or `self.param = param or []` in an operator __init__ where an explicit empty list means something downstream.
clusters.rationale: Airflow's domain is full of meaningful zeros and empty values - map_index 0, an XCom of False, an empty list that clears permissions - and a truthiness check silently turns each of them into `not supplied`.

clusters.rule: Add every related object to the session first and flush once at the end rather than flushing part-way through, in production write paths and test setup alike, unless a later setup query genuinely needs the earlier flush.
clusters.trigger: A session.flush() call appears mid-function inside write_dag or a similar multi-object DB write before all related objects have been added, or two or more session.flush() calls appear in the setup section of one test function or fixture.
clusters.rationale: Each flush is a round trip and a partial write; batching them into one keeps the unit of work atomic and keeps the query counts Airflow asserts on predictable.

clusters.rule: Make UI HTTP calls through the generated React Query layer - the OpenAPI-generated react-query hooks in airflow-core, useQuery/useMutation over Axios in the Edge plugin UI - never a raw fetch or a direct axios call from a component.
clusters.trigger: A .tsx component or a file under airflow-core/src/airflow/ui/src/queries/ calls fetch on an OpenAPI.BASE template string, builds a query string with manual encodeURIComponent/join, or calls axios.get/axios.post directly.
clusters.rationale: The generated hooks carry auth, caching, invalidation and the API's own types; a hand-rolled call re-implements all of that and drifts the moment the spec changes.

clusters.rule: Tie a new migration to the next unreleased version: an airflow-core migration adds its _REVISION_HEADS_MAP entry under that version and keeps the map chaining monotonically through the previous head, and a provider migration file is named for the next unreleased provider version - rename it before merge if a new minor has been cut since the branch opened.
clusters.trigger: A migration is added under airflow/migrations/ with no _REVISION_HEADS_MAP entry, or with an entry under an already-released version key or one whose down_revision does not follow the previous head; or a file under providers/*/migrations/versions/ embeds a version string at or below the latest release.
clusters.rationale: The revision map and the migration file names are how Airflow works out which schema belongs to which release; pointing a migration at a version that has already shipped means users upgrading to it never run it.

clusters.rule: Never log or print a connection, its URI, or any credential string - at any log level, including temporary debug prints; redact the value or use the security code-scanning suppression first.
clusters.trigger: A log. or print( call in airflow-core or under task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/execution_time/ takes a Connection, a ConnectionResult, Connection.get_uri() output, a password or another secret as its argument.
clusters.rationale: Task and execution logs are persisted and shipped to remote backends users can read; one URI in a log line hands a live credential to everyone with log access.

clusters.rule: airflow-core, including its tests, must not import Task SDK internals: no airflow.sdk._shared or other private SDK namespaces, and no exception from airflow/sdk/exceptions.py that is only raised inside the SDK - those tests belong in the SDK test tree.
clusters.trigger: An import in airflow-core source or airflow-core/tests/ changes from airflow.X to airflow.sdk._shared.X or another airflow.sdk internal namespace, or pulls a Task-SDK-only exception from airflow.sdk.exceptions.
clusters.rationale: The Task SDK ships and versions separately from airflow-core; every core import of an SDK-private path pins the two together and stops the SDK moving its own internals.

clusters.rule: Put imports at module scope; an import inside a function, method, test helper or fixture body is acceptable only to break a genuine circular import or for deliberate lazy loading (worker isolation, TYPE_CHECKING), and must carry a comment naming the reason.
clusters.trigger: An import or from-import statement appears inside a function, method, test helper or fixture body with no adjacent comment explaining the circular-import or lazy-loading reason.
clusters.rationale: Function-body imports hide real dependency cycles and cost on every call; without the comment the next reader cannot tell whether the placement is load-bearing or accidental, so nobody ever moves it back.

clusters.rule: Measure deadlines and elapsed durations in triggers and operators with time.monotonic(), and build the deadline values in their tests with that same clock.
clusters.trigger: time.time() is used to compute or compare a deadline or elapsed duration inside a Trigger or Operator, or a test constructs a deadline such as END_TIME = time.time() + ... for a trigger whose implementation reads time.monotonic().
clusters.rationale: The wall clock jumps on NTP correction, which silently expires or extends a trigger's timeout; and a test that mixes the two clocks compares unrelated origins, so it passes or fails for reasons unrelated to the code.

clusters.rule: Do not reach for pytest's caplog to prove behaviour: assert on observable behaviour or return values, and in Kubernetes and integration tests capture log output with mocks instead.
clusters.trigger: A test imports or takes the caplog fixture to assert on logged messages, or a test under kubernetes-tests/ takes caplog as a parameter or fixture.
clusters.rationale: Log text is not the contract and changes freely; caplog also cannot see output from the separate processes Kubernetes and integration tests drive, so those assertions pass or fail for the wrong reasons.

clusters.rule: Keep the public surface of provider operators, hooks, executors and extractors backward compatible: a renamed attribute or method keeps a deprecated forwarding property, a removed parameter is deprecated with its values mapped onto the replacement, and a changed return value, changed traversal or new constructor keyword is opt-in through a parameter that defaults to the existing behaviour.
clusters.trigger: A diff renames a public attribute or method on a BaseExecutor subclass with no shim, removes an operator parameter such as wait_policy and hard-codes one of its former values, changes an existing operator's execute() return shape, alters what an existing hook method traverses or returns, or passes a new required keyword to a subclass constructor such as BaseExtractor.__init__ unconditionally.
clusters.rationale: Provider packages are consumed by DAGs and subclasses Airflow cannot see or update; a silent change to the public surface breaks them at runtime in someone else's deployment, with no deprecation cycle to warn them.

clusters.rule: Expose a value callers need to control - an operation timeout, a flag the paired trigger consumes - as a constructor parameter on the operator or hook and pass it through, instead of hard-coding it at the construction site or fixing it in a module-level constant.
clusters.trigger: A trigger is instantiated with a boolean argument such as cancel_on_kill that is not exposed as a parameter on the enclosing operator, or a module-level *_TIMEOUT constant gates a long-running provider API call with no matching constructor parameter.
clusters.rationale: DAG authors tune these per workload; a value baked into the operator body can only be changed by forking it, so reviewers treat it as a missing parameter rather than a default.

clusters.rule: A provider must not reach for an airflow-core symbol or attribute that does not exist in its minimum supported core version: guard the import behind a version or ImportError check, and read a newer attribute with getattr(obj, 'attr', default) rather than accessing it directly.
clusters.trigger: An unconditional import of a new airflow-core symbol in a provider whose min_ver predates it, or direct attribute access on a core object for an attribute added after the provider's minimum supported Airflow version.
clusters.rationale: A provider release installs against every core version in its supported range; an unguarded reference becomes an ImportError or AttributeError at DAG parse time on the oldest supported core, long after the provider was published.

clusters.rule: Raise the native Python exception that fits - ValueError, TypeError, RuntimeError - for argument validation, bad user input, unexpected internal state and third-party service failures in provider code and triggers, rather than AirflowException.
clusters.trigger: A new `raise AirflowException(...)` for parameter validation inside a provider hook or operator, for an internal error condition inside a BaseTrigger.run() coroutine, or for an error that originated in an external service.
clusters.rationale: AirflowException means Airflow itself decided to fail; using it for everything strips the type information callers branch on and makes a vendor API error indistinguishable from a scheduler failure.

clusters.rule: In a deferrable operator, persist operator links and push the job or query identifier to XCom as soon as it is obtained - before self.defer() and before entering any polling loop - not after the wait completes.
clusters.trigger: A self.persist() or link-persistence call, or an xcom_push for a query/job id, is placed after a self.defer(...) call or after the polling loop in a deferrable operator's execute().
clusters.rationale: Once the task defers, execute() never resumes at that point, so anything pushed afterwards is never written; users also need the job id while the task is still running in order to find it in the vendor console.

clusters.rule: A trigger's run() must yield a distinct terminal TriggerEvent for every terminal condition it can reach: separate success and failure events rather than one collapsed success, and a timeout event carrying the timeout status and a descriptive reason rather than a bare break or return - with any cancellation side-effect in the timeout branch wrapped in its own try/except so a failed cancel cannot replace the event.
clusters.trigger: An `async def run()` yields a TriggerEvent with no separate success/failure handling or compares status against a single string instead of the provider's Enum, or a polling loop in providers/*/triggers/*.py reaches its timeout condition and breaks without yielding, or performs a cancel call in the timeout branch outside a dedicated try/except.
clusters.rationale: The triggerer only learns what happened from the event: a loop that exits without yielding leaves the task hanging, and a failure reported as success sends the DAG down the wrong path.

clusters.rule: Every package a provider imports directly must be declared as a direct dependency in that provider's pyproject.toml, in the same PR as the import; do not rely on it arriving transitively.
clusters.trigger: An `import <package>` under providers/<name>/src/ where <package> is absent from dependencies or the relevant extra in providers/<name>/pyproject.toml.
clusters.rationale: Providers are installed standalone, and a transitive dependency disappears the moment the intermediate package drops it - the failure then surfaces as an ImportError in a user's deployment rather than in CI.

clusters.rule: Annotate a provider compatibility shim with the Airflow version it is tied to: an ImportError fallback for a Task SDK symbol names the minimum >=X.Y.Z release that exports it, and a workaround for an older core API carries a `# TODO: Remove once minimum supported Airflow version is X.Y` comment.
clusters.trigger: A `try: from airflow.sdk... except ImportError: Symbol = None` block, or a version-compat override or workaround block, is added in a provider with no comment naming the version that introduces the symbol or retires the shim.
clusters.rationale: Shims outlive the versions they were written for; without the version in the comment nobody can tell when it became safe to delete, so the workarounds accumulate for years.

clusters.rule: When a provider operator or hook gains a new parameter or changes its documented behaviour, update the class docstring - a `:param name:` entry describing the type, and for a Callable what each positional argument means - and the matching provider RST guide, in the same PR.
clusters.trigger: A new keyword argument on a provider operator or hook __init__ (e.g. KubernetesPodOperator) with no corresponding `:param:` entry, or a new or changed `:param ...:` list with no edit to providers/<name>/docs/operators/*.rst or providers/<name>/docs/connections/*.rst.
clusters.rationale: The published provider docs are generated from these two sources and are the only thing DAG authors see; a parameter documented in neither place effectively does not exist for users.

clusters.rule: Add a bullet to a provider's changelog.rst only when that provider's own source files change: a PR touching only test files, another provider's tests, or non-functional pyproject.toml marker comments gets no entry or release section.
clusters.trigger: A new bullet or version section in providers/<name>/docs/changelog.rst for a diff whose changed files are all under tests/, belong to a different provider, or are only `# use next version` comments.
clusters.rationale: The changelog is what users read to decide whether to upgrade; entries for changes with no runtime effect make every release look risky and bury the ones that matter.

clusters.rule: Everything belonging to a provider lives inside that provider's own directory: its prek/pre-commit hooks and their supporting scripts under providers/<name>/, and its logo and image assets under providers/<name>/ rather than a parallel top-level folder.
clusters.trigger: A hook entry in a provider hatch_build.py or provider hook config points at a script outside providers/<name>/, or image and logo files are added under registry/ instead of providers/<name>/.
clusters.rationale: Providers are extracted and released as standalone distributions; anything of theirs sitting at the repository root is left behind by that split and ends up with no owner.

clusters.rule: Do not perform per-row database work inside a loop over DAGs, task instances or task-map entries: hoist the query outside the loop, batch it, or pass the already-fetched data in; if the data comes from a SQLAlchemy relationship, eager-load it instead of touching the attribute lazily inside the loop.
clusters.trigger: A session.scalars()/session.execute()/session.scalar() call, or a dotted lazy relationship access (e.g. record.dataset.uri), appears inside a for-loop over dags_needing_dagruns, dataset_triggered_dag_info, or mapped task instances.
clusters.rationale: The scheduler and task-mapping loops run per DAG and per task instance on every scheduling cycle, so one extra query or one lazy load inside the loop becomes an N+1 that scales with the size of the deployment.

clusters.rule: In hot-path queries, select only the columns actually used rather than the whole ORM entity: grid and UI endpoints must enumerate their columns instead of select(TaskInstance)/select(DagRun), and with_row_locks selects must fetch only the primary key when only the id is used.
clusters.trigger: A query on a grid/UI endpoint uses select(SomeModel) instead of listing columns, or a with_row_locks(select(AssetModel).where(...)) retrieves the full model when only .id is consumed.
clusters.rationale: Selecting whole ORM rows pulls back columns nobody reads and, for locking selects, widens the lock beyond an index scan; these endpoints and code paths are the ones that hurt at scale.

clusters.rule: Import symbols that have been migrated to the Task SDK from their airflow.sdk.* public path, not from the legacy airflow-core module (e.g. XCOM_RETURN_KEY from the Task SDK BaseXCom rather than airflow.models.xcom; exceptions from airflow.sdk.exceptions rather than airflow.exceptions).
clusters.trigger: A file, docs example or provider imports a symbol from airflow.models.xcom / airflow.exceptions (often with a `# type: ignore[no-redef]`) when the same symbol is already exported by airflow.sdk.*.
clusters.rationale: Task-facing code must not depend on airflow-core internals; the SDK path is the supported surface and the legacy path is being removed.

clusters.rule: Do not grant the token:workload scope on state-changing execution-API routes; restrict token:workload to read-only endpoints (GET variable/keys, GET/HEAD xcom, GET connection, GET dag_run) and keep PUT/POST/DELETE routes token:execution only.
clusters.trigger: A router.put/post/delete endpoint in the execution API declares Security(require_auth, scopes=[..., "token:workload"]), or a has_variable_access / has_xcom_access dependency on a write route is replaced by a workload-inclusive scope list.
clusters.rationale: The workload token is long-lived and low-privilege; widening it to mutations lets a worker hold write authority for far longer than the execution token it should be using.

clusters.rule: In SQLAlchemy 2.0 declarative models the Mapped[...] annotation is authoritative for nullability: it must agree with the column's nullable setting, and a redundant nullable=True kwarg must not be passed alongside Mapped[X | None].
clusters.trigger: A mapped_column(...) carries nullable=True while its annotation is Mapped[X | None], or a Mapped[X | None] annotation sits on a column declared nullable=False (or vice versa).
clusters.rationale: The annotation is what type checkers and readers trust; a mismatch between it and the column definition is a silent lie about the schema.

clusters.rule: Keep a PR scoped to the change its title and description claim: unrelated uv.lock churn must be reverted, an Alembic migration that fixes a pre-existing schema issue must go in its own PR, and a second independent feature must either be split out or added to the PR description with its own rationale and compatibility notes.
clusters.trigger: The diff contains uv.lock changes with no dependency bump in the description, an independent schema-fix migration alongside a feature migration, or a second unrelated feature (e.g. worker recycling added to a DAG-caching PR).
clusters.rationale: Reviewers approve what the description says; bundled unrelated changes get merged unreviewed and cannot be reverted independently when one of them regresses.

clusters.rule: Help text for CLI date arguments that filter runs by partition or logical date must state the exact semantics: whether the end bound is inclusive or exclusive (and what value covers a whole calendar period), and that the calendar day is derived from the UTC instant rather than the user's local or the timetable's timezone.
clusters.trigger: A CLI argument in cli_config.py / dag_command.py adds --start-date / --end-date (or another type=parsedate date filter) whose help text does not spell out inclusivity and the UTC-day interpretation.
clusters.rationale: Ambiguity between midnight-on-the-last-day and first-of-next-month, or a tz-aware input shifting the interpreted day, causes silent data loss the user only notices later.

clusters.rule: Changes to callback execution must be applied to both the executor path and the triggerer path so the two stay behaviourally identical: a new context key must be added via the shared build_context_from_dag_run helper (and declared in the Context TypedDict and KNOWN_CONTEXT_KEYS), and both paths must fail the same way when required context such as the DagRun cannot be fetched.
clusters.trigger: callback_supervisor.py populates context or handles a fetch failure differently from the corresponding build_context_from_dag_run / context-fetch code in triggerer_job_runner.py (e.g. one returns None while the other raises or exits).
clusters.rationale: Callbacks can run on either path; divergence means a callback silently sees different context or keeps running with None instead of retrying, depending on where it happened to be scheduled.

clusters.rule: New or changed behaviour on a public API endpoint must be covered by tests asserting the new response, including the new validation error path and the changed default.
clusters.trigger: A bulk endpoint gains a validation guard, or a service method changes what an endpoint returns by default, without new or updated tests for those paths.
clusters.rationale: Reviewers asked for the tests because the new branch was otherwise unexercised.

clusters.rule: Bulk endpoints must enforce the same authorization and state guards as their single-item counterparts: shared helpers must take the HTTP method as a parameter instead of hardcoding "PUT", and handle_bulk_delete must apply the single-delete state checks unless the relaxation is documented and intentional.
clusters.trigger: A shared authorization helper (e.g. _categorize_entities) hardcodes method="PUT" but is called from a bulk-delete path, or handle_bulk_delete omits a guard the single-delete route applies (e.g. refusing RUNNING DagRuns).
clusters.rationale: The bulk route is the easy way around the single-item route; if it is laxer, the guards on the single-item endpoint are decorative.

clusters.rule: Every actions/upload-artifact step in a GitHub Actions job must use a unique artifact name, including names built from a shared dynamic suffix.
clusters.trigger: Two or more upload-artifact steps in the same job share a name: value or the same name template (e.g. both container-logs-${{env.JOB_ID}}).
clusters.rationale: Duplicate artifact names make the second upload clobber or fail against the first, so the logs the step exists to preserve are lost exactly when a job failed.

clusters.rule: Task-SDK client changelog entries belong in the Task-SDK changelog, not in the airflow-core RELEASE_NOTES.rst.
clusters.trigger: RELEASE_NOTES.rst gains a line mentioning task-sdk / Task SDK client inside an airflow-core section.
clusters.rationale: The distributions release on separate cycles; an entry in the wrong changelog tells users a change shipped in a version that does not contain it.

clusters.rule: A database migration shipped in a patch release may only repair a bug in an existing migration; it must not change payload semantics such that users who already ran the original upgrade end up in a different state from a fresh install.
clusters.trigger: A patch-release PR modifies a file under migrations/versions/ and changes upgrade()/downgrade() logic beyond a no-op correction.
clusters.rationale: Patch releases are applied by users who have already migrated; divergent end states between upgraded and fresh installs are undetectable and unfixable after the fact.

clusters.rule: A new config option introduced in a patch release must be declared in config.yml and explicitly called out in that minor version's upgrade notes.
clusters.trigger: A patch PR adds a key to config.yml, or documents a new [section] key_name, with no corresponding entry in the upgrade notes.
clusters.rationale: Operators read upgrade notes to decide whether a patch is safe; a silently added option changes behaviour they never opted into.

clusters.rule: A reusable workflow whose workflow_dispatch trigger is gated by a committer allowlist must apply the same allowlist check to its workflow_call trigger.
clusters.trigger: A workflow defines a committer-restricted workflow_dispatch block but exposes workflow_call without an equivalent contains(fromJSON([...]), github.event.sender.login) guard.
clusters.rationale: Otherwise any caller workflow bypasses the gate entirely, which is exactly the escalation the allowlist exists to prevent.

clusters.rule: Provider governance documentation must not state that a sponsoring committer is absolved of technical responsibility for the PRs they merge; committers remain responsible for CI health and security review regardless of steward approval.
clusters.trigger: PROVIDERS.rst or an equivalent governance document says the sponsor is NOT responsible for the codebase or for merged PRs.
clusters.rationale: Merge rights carry ASF accountability; wording that disclaims it invites unreviewed provider code into the release.

clusters.rule: Illustrate provider policy concepts in governance documentation with vendor-neutral examples (e.g. the http provider) rather than a named commercial vendor.
clusters.trigger: PROVIDERS.rst or a provider governance document uses a specific vendor name (Slack, AWS, GCP) as the sole illustrative example of a policy.
clusters.rationale: Naming one vendor in policy text reads as a statement about that vendor's standing in the project.

clusters.rule: Every locale skill file under .github/skills/airflow-translations/locales/ must declare that it extends the global rules in ../SKILL.md and that the locale file takes precedence on conflict.
clusters.trigger: A locale skill file (.github/skills/airflow-translations/locales/<lang>.md) is added or modified without a reference to ../SKILL.md and an explicit precedence statement.
clusters.rationale: Without the precedence statement a translator cannot tell which rule wins when the global and locale guidance disagree.

clusters.rule: In a locale's do-not-translate list, mark only the bare Airflow noun (e.g. "Asset") as untranslatable; do not block compound phrases (e.g. "Asset Events") whose surrounding words the existing locale JSON already translates.
clusters.trigger: A locale skill file's do-not-translate list contains a multi-word phrase built around an Airflow term while the locale's JSON files translate the non-Airflow words of that phrase.
clusters.rationale: Blocking the compound contradicts the translations already shipped for that locale and makes the skill file unusable as written.

clusters.rule: Documentation for extensible Airflow interfaces (state backends, secrets backends, other plug points) must describe the contract and behaviour rather than enumerate concrete method signatures.
clusters.trigger: A .rst file adds a list-table or code-block of full method signatures (e.g. async def ...) for a pluggable backend or extension point.
clusters.rationale: Signatures change between releases; documented ones go stale immediately and mislead implementers.

clusters.rule: A CI shell script that starts `airflow standalone` in the background and polls for readiness must check liveness with `kill -0 $AIRFLOW_PID` so it exits as soon as the process dies instead of waiting out the full timeout.
clusters.trigger: A CI script launches airflow standalone in the background, captures its PID, then polls in a timed loop with no kill -0 $AIRFLOW_PID check.
clusters.rationale: Without the liveness check a crashed standalone burns the whole timeout on every CI run and reports a timeout instead of the real failure.

clusters.rule: AIP skill SKILL.md files must anchor AIP URL detection to the Apache Confluence prefix https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/AIRFLOW rather than treating any https:// argument as the AIP URL.
clusters.trigger: A SKILL.md under .github/skills/aip-* describes AIP URL detection as "other https:// arguments are the AIP URL" with no cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/AIRFLOW anchor.
clusters.rationale: An unanchored pattern makes the skill fetch arbitrary URLs the user passed for another purpose.

clusters.rule: Locale skill files must cross-reference the rationale already documented in airflow-core/src/airflow/ui/public/i18n/locales/<lang>/README.md when they consolidate that locale's translation conventions.
clusters.trigger: A locale skill file under .github/skills/airflow-translations/locales/ is created or updated with no reference to the in-tree i18n README for that locale.
clusters.rationale: The README holds the reasoning the locale's translators already agreed on; a skill file that restates conventions without pointing at it will drift from them.

clusters.rule: Docs examples showing regex filtering of asset partition keys must call .partition_key_pattern(), not .partition_key() (which is exact-match).
clusters.trigger: A docs example passes a regex string to .partition_key(.
clusters.rationale: The example as written silently does an exact-match comparison and never fires.

clusters.rule: Documentation for a feature introduced in a specific Airflow version must get its own .. note:: block or subheader rather than being nested under a section that documents a different feature.
clusters.trigger: A diff adds documentation for a new feature (e.g. Resumable Tasks) inside an existing section covering a distinct feature (e.g. Deferred Operators).
clusters.rationale: Readers scanning for the section's subject skip past the buried feature, and version applicability gets attached to the wrong thing.

clusters.rule: Derive component versions such as TASK_SDK_VERSION from PACKAGE_VERSION with packaging.version.parse_version() and its .minor/.micro attributes, never by splitting the version string on ".".
clusters.trigger: PACKAGE_VERSION.split('.') is used to derive a version component.
clusters.rationale: String splitting breaks on pre-release, dev and post suffixes that the project's versions actually carry.

clusters.rule: Auth-manager documentation must reference get_url_refresh() for the token-refresh endpoint rather than hardcoding a literal path such as POST /auth/token/refresh.
clusters.trigger: Documentation hardcodes an auth token refresh URL path instead of pointing at the get_url_refresh method.
clusters.rationale: The path is auth-manager specific; a hardcoded one is wrong for every manager that overrides it.

clusters.rule: Airflow documentation must describe the current behaviour without comparing it to earlier versions; drop phrases like "no longer", "previously", "used to" and "as of version X".
clusters.trigger: Documentation prose adds "no longer", "previously", "used to", or "as of Airflow X.Y".
clusters.rationale: Docs are versioned; historical comparison belongs in release notes and rots in place in the guide.

clusters.rule: Document task-state-store and asset-state-store values as JsonValue (any JSON-serialisable type), not as strings.
clusters.trigger: Docs describe a task store or asset store value type as "string"/"str" rather than JsonValue or JSON.
clusters.rationale: The stores accept arbitrary JSON; documenting them as strings makes users serialise by hand.

clusters.rule: Authentication documentation must not present the FAB Auth Manager as the default; the default auth manager in Airflow 3 is the Simple Auth Manager.
clusters.trigger: Docs or configuration examples imply the FAB Auth Manager is in use by default.
clusters.rationale: FAB moved to a provider in Airflow 3; examples assuming it fail on a stock install.

clusters.rule: Getting-started and quickstart documentation must cover both the uv-based install path and the standard pip + venv path.
clusters.trigger: The install quickstart section is added or rewritten covering only uv or only pip.
clusters.rationale: Newcomers arrive with whichever tool they already have; a single-tool quickstart blocks the other half of them.

clusters.rule: Use a bugfix.rst newsfragment rather than significant.rst for internal fixes with no observable user-facing behaviour change, and omit the fragment entirely when there is no user impact.
clusters.trigger: A significant.rst newsfragment is added for an internal race-condition fix or scheduler-internal improvement with no API or behaviour change.
clusters.rationale: Significant fragments are read as migration-relevant; filling them with internal churn buries the entries that actually require action.

clusters.rule: A significant newsfragment describing a permission or endpoint change must name the surface precisely (e.g. "FastAPI UI /dags endpoint") to distinguish it from other endpoints sharing the same path.
clusters.trigger: A significant.rst newsfragment mentions /dags or another ambiguous path without saying whether it is the UI route or the public REST API endpoint.
clusters.rationale: Operators decide whether the change affects them from this line alone, and the two surfaces have different audiences.

clusters.rule: Do not enable asyncio debug logging in production code paths or default configuration.
clusters.trigger: PYTHONASYNCIODEBUG, loop.set_debug(True), or asyncio debug logging is enabled in non-test code.
clusters.rationale: Asyncio debug output includes coroutine arguments, which puts connection credentials into task logs.

clusters.rule: Do not add native/binary C-extension libraries to the mandatory dependencies of airflow-core; they belong in an optional extra or a provider.
clusters.trigger: A library distributed only as a compiled wheel, with no pure-Python fallback, is added to the dependencies list in airflow-core/pyproject.toml.
clusters.rationale: Core must install on every platform and Python build the project supports; a mandatory binary wheel makes core uninstallable wherever it has no wheel.

clusters.rule: is_authorized_* methods on BaseAuthManager and its subclasses must take the generic auth-user type-var (user: T) and express multiple user ids as set[str]; they must not accept concrete Airflow model types such as HITLUser.
clusters.trigger: An is_authorized_* method is added or modified on an auth manager taking a concrete Airflow model type instead of user: T or primitives.
clusters.rationale: BaseAuthManager is implemented outside the repo; binding its signatures to core models forces every third-party auth manager to import them.

clusters.rule: Extend an existing is_authorized_* method with an optional parameter rather than adding a parallel is_authorized_<action>_for_<entity> method to the BaseAuthManager interface.
clusters.trigger: A new method matching is_authorized_.*_for_ is added to BaseAuthManager.
clusters.rationale: Every method on this interface must be implemented by every downstream auth manager, so the interface has to stay small.

clusters.rule: Do not set document.title from inside React components in the Airflow UI; the title is defined once in index.html.
clusters.trigger: A document.title assignment appears inside a useEffect in a .tsx file under the Airflow UI source tree.
clusters.rationale: Per-page title juggling in components fights the single definition and leaves stale titles when the component unmounts.

clusters.rule: Resolve the authenticated user through resolve_user_from_token (core_api/security.py) rather than calling get_auth_manager().get_user_from_token directly from middleware or route code.
clusters.trigger: A direct get_auth_manager().get_user_from_token( call appears outside resolve_user_from_token.
clusters.rationale: resolve_user_from_token carries the error translation and validation every caller needs; bypassing it produces routes that authenticate slightly differently.

clusters.rule: Name JWT duration parameters valid_for (a relative duration); do not call them expiry or expires_at, which imply an absolute timestamp.
clusters.trigger: A JWT-generation method takes a parameter named expiry or expires_at whose value is actually a TTL integer or timedelta.
clusters.rationale: Callers pass what the name says; an absolute-sounding name receiving a TTL produces tokens with wildly wrong lifetimes.

clusters.rule: Keyset cursor pagination over a nullable sort column must use null-aware comparisons (an IS NULL tie-break or COALESCE) that match the ORDER BY null-ordering semantics.
clusters.trigger: Cursor code appends and_(*eq_conditions, col > value) for a column that can be NULL without an IS NULL guard.
clusters.rationale: col > NULL is never true, so rows with a null sort key silently vanish from or terminate the paging sequence.

clusters.rule: Use if/elif rather than consecutive if statements for the mutually exclusive lower_bound / lower_bound_excluded filter branches so the query does not emit redundant WHERE clauses.
clusters.trigger: Two consecutive `if self.value and self.value.lower_bound...` blocks appear for bound conditions that cannot both apply.
clusters.rationale: The reviewer pointed out that both branches can run and add duplicate predicates.

clusters.rule: Annotate DAG-bearing attributes in API parameter and datamodel classes as SerializedDAG (imported under TYPE_CHECKING from airflow.serialization.serialized_objects) rather than Any.
clusters.trigger: A property or attribute in a parameter/datamodel class is typed None | Any where the value is a serialized DAG.
clusters.rationale: Any here hides the one type the code actually depends on and defeats the type checking these modules otherwise get.

clusters.rule: Queries built from _RegexParam must be wrapped with apply_regex_query_timeout, and the _RegexParam docstring must state that obligation.
clusters.trigger: A route uses _RegexParam or regex_param_factory without a corresponding apply_regex_query_timeout call, or a _RegexParam class/factory has no docstring warning about it.
clusters.rationale: User-supplied regexes can be catastrophically slow in the database; the timeout is the only thing keeping one request from occupying a connection indefinitely.

clusters.rule: In SortParam.get_resolved_columns(), derive attr_name after applying to_replace so the resolved name matches the ORM attribute used in ORDER BY and cursor encoding.
clusters.trigger: attr_name = lstriped_orderby is assigned before the to_replace mapping is applied.
clusters.rationale: The reviewer caught the ordering defect: the encoded cursor referred to a column the ORDER BY did not use.

clusters.rule: When a Pydantic validator silently coerces an unrecognised stored value to None, emit a log.warning so schema drift between the server and the database stays observable.
clusters.trigger: `except ValidationError: return None` in a Pydantic validator with no preceding log.warning when the value was not already None.
clusters.rationale: Silent coercion turns a schema mismatch into an empty field in the UI with nothing anywhere indicating why.

clusters.rule: Boolean timetable properties consumed by the API (e.g. is_backfillable) must be persisted as a DagModel column via a migration, not derived at runtime by matching timetable_summary strings.
clusters.trigger: A frozenset of timetable summary strings is used in a datamodel or route to derive a boolean DAG property instead of reading a DagModel column.
clusters.rationale: Summary strings are display text from arbitrary timetables, including third-party ones; matching on them silently misclassifies any timetable not in the list.

clusters.rule: When redacting a dict value in an API response serializer, keep it a JSON-serialisable dict rather than wrapping the result in str().
clusters.trigger: str(redact(value)) where value is a dict in a Pydantic response serializer or validator.
clusters.rationale: Stringifying turns structured trigger kwargs into a Python repr the client has to parse, and it leaks into the public schema.

clusters.rule: Partition-date-window localization implemented inline in a route must not silently use a different interval convention from DagRun.apply_partition_date_window; consolidate the logic or cross-reference it in a comment.
clusters.trigger: An inline timetable.localize_partition_datetime call in a route duplicates DagRun.apply_partition_date_window with a different inclusive/half-open boundary.
clusters.rationale: The reviewer noticed the two copies had already drifted on the interval boundary.

clusters.rule: Validate that a requested try_number exists in the database before using it to build extra links, and return 404 when it does not.
clusters.trigger: ti.try_number = try_number is assigned in an extra-links route with no preceding check that the try number exists.
clusters.rationale: Without the check the endpoint renders links for a try that never ran, which look valid to the caller.

clusters.rule: Do not name a variable task_instance when it may hold either a TaskInstance or a TaskInstanceHistory; use a neutral name such as row, entity, or model.
clusters.trigger: A variable named task_instance is assigned from a query that can return either TI or TIH ORM objects.
clusters.rationale: The two models have overlapping but different attributes; the name tells the next reader they can rely on TI behaviour that may not be there.

clusters.rule: Define callback-definition objects such as _ImportPathCallbackDef in the domain model module (e.g. models/test_connection.py) rather than constructing them inline in a route handler.
clusters.trigger: An _ImportPathCallbackDef or ExecutorCallback construction is inlined inside a route handler body.
clusters.rationale: The callback definition is part of the domain contract executors consume; keeping it in the route makes it unreachable from every other caller.

clusters.rule: Use entity.name when collecting pool names in bulk-action validation; check attribute names against the actual Pydantic body class before building error lists.
clusters.trigger: invalid_entities.append(entity.pool) or a similar wrong attribute access on a PoolBody instance in bulk-action validation.
clusters.rationale: PoolBody has no such attribute, so the validation path raises instead of reporting the invalid entities.

clusters.rule: Cursor-paginated endpoints must fetch limit+1 rows to detect whether another page exists, and return next_cursor as null when it does not.
clusters.trigger: A paginated endpoint computes next_cursor/previous_cursor from the current page slice without fetching a probe row.
clusters.rationale: Without the probe row the last page still advertises a next cursor, so clients keep paging into an empty response.

clusters.rule: Tests for a cursor-paginated route must assert both boundaries: previous_cursor is null on the first page and next_cursor is null on the last.
clusters.trigger: A new cursor-pagination route is added without tests covering previous_cursor on page 1 and next_cursor on the final page.
clusters.rationale: These are the two cases clients depend on to terminate iteration, and the ones most often wrong.

clusters.rule: PATCH routes that honour update_mask must return HTTP 422 when a field named in update_mask has a null value in the request body.
clusters.trigger: A PATCH handler iterates fields_to_update/update_mask without validating that each included field carries a non-null value.
clusters.rationale: Passing the null downstream writes a null the client did not intend, instead of telling them the request was malformed.

clusters.rule: Do not add CASE expressions to a query's ORDER BY to force NULL ordering; rely on the database's default NULL ordering so the sort can use an index.
clusters.trigger: A SQLAlchemy query adds a CASE expression in ORDER BY to place NULLs first or last.
clusters.rationale: A computed ORDER BY key makes the index unusable and turns a paged list query into a full sort.

clusters.rule: Parallel EXISTS subquery predicates on the grid endpoint (e.g. has_note, has_missed_deadline) must use identical filter conditions for their DagRun and TaskInstance counterparts.
clusters.trigger: A subquery EXISTS predicate on DagRunNote differs in its filtering (e.g. an extra .isnot(None)) from the TaskInstanceNote version.
clusters.rationale: The reviewer found the two note filters had diverged so the grid reported notes differently for runs and task instances.

clusters.rule: Every new router included in the execution API's authenticated_router must have a matching endpoint(...).didnt_exist entry in the unreleased Cadwyn version file.
clusters.trigger: A new router is added to authenticated_router.include_router() in execution_api/routes/__init__.py with no corresponding didnt_exist entry in versions/v*.py.
clusters.rationale: Cadwyn generates the older API versions from those declarations; a missing entry silently exposes the new endpoint on versions that predate it.

clusters.rule: A new state table keyed on an asset must come with a decided lifecycle for its rows when the corresponding AssetActive row is removed - a cascade delete or an explicit GC policy - not unbounded accumulation.
clusters.trigger: A new asset_state table/model is introduced with no cascade-delete from AssetActive removal and no GC policy.
clusters.rationale: Orphaned state rows in the metadata database are never cleaned up by anything else and grow without limit.

clusters.rule: Do not add a field to a Pydantic response model whose name is the singular or plural variant of an existing field unless the two have clearly distinct, documented semantics.
clusters.trigger: A Pydantic model gains a field whose name is the plural (or singular) form of an existing field, e.g. partition_key alongside partition_keys.
clusters.rationale: API consumers cannot tell the two apart from the schema, and client code picks the wrong one.

clusters.rule: Do not drive a single-item state operation through the bulk service interface; use the single-item service code path.
clusters.trigger: A non-bulk route instantiates a BulkService with a dummy empty BulkBody to perform a single-item update.
clusters.rationale: The bulk service carries per-entry error accumulation and partial-success semantics that make no sense for one item and obscure the real failure mode.

clusters.rule: When a new conditional branch is added in a service method, update the response-serialisation helper to cover it so the branch is not dead code.
clusters.trigger: A new query branch is added in a service method while _serialize_response (or equivalent) still gates on the old condition.
clusters.rationale: The reviewer found the new branch was unreachable in the response as written.

clusters.rule: Assign a large dict to a named variable before passing it to Model.model_validate() rather than inlining the literal in the call.
clusters.trigger: Model.model_validate({...}) is called with a multi-key inline dict containing computed or conditional expressions.
clusters.rationale: Readability nit raised on one call site.

clusters.rule: Do not use getattr(Model, "field") in SQLAlchemy column-selection expressions; resolve optional or dynamically named columns inside the model definition instead.
clusters.trigger: A select() call references a column via getattr(SomeModel, "column_name").
clusters.rationale: The string reference is invisible to type checkers and to any rename, so the query breaks at runtime long after the model changed.

clusters.rule: Do not call session.flush() from a finally or except block reached on an error path.
clusters.trigger: session.flush() is added inside a finally: or except: clause in an asset or scheduler code path.
clusters.rationale: The transaction is about to roll back, so the flush accomplishes nothing except obscuring the error handling.

clusters.rule: On the /run endpoint, mint a new execution token only when the incoming token is workload-scoped; do not regenerate a token on every call.
clusters.trigger: Unconditional generator.generate(extras={"scope": "execution"}) plus a response.headers["Refreshed-API-Token"] assignment inside the ti_run handler with no scope guard.
clusters.rationale: Unconditional reissue replaces tokens that still have more validity left and bypasses the JWTReissueMiddleware 20%-remaining rule that governs refresh everywhere else.

clusters.rule: When a route handler writes the Refreshed-API-Token header that JWTReissueMiddleware also writes, add an inline comment explaining why they cannot collide.
clusters.trigger: response.headers["Refreshed-API-Token"] is assigned in a route handler that coexists with JWTReissueMiddleware.
clusters.rationale: The reviewer asked for the non-collision contract to be written down at the second writer.

clusters.rule: Generate the execution JWT before the transition to the running state is committed.
clusters.trigger: generator.generate() or the Refreshed-API-Token assignment is placed after the session.commit()/session.flush() that moves the TI to running.
clusters.rationale: If token generation fails after the commit, the task instance is stuck in running with no execution token and the worker has no way to recover it.

clusters.rule: Keep JWT and token-generation code outside `except SQLAlchemyError` blocks in execution-API route handlers; the DB error handler must cover only database operations.
clusters.trigger: services.aget(JWTGenerator) or generator.generate() is placed inside a try/except SQLAlchemyError block in an execution API route.
clusters.rationale: Widening the try block means a signing failure is reported as a database error, and the DB-specific recovery runs for something that was never a DB problem.

clusters.rule: Every new router in the execution API must set route_class=ExecutionAPIRoute.
clusters.trigger: A new VersionedAPIRouter(...) is added under execution_api/routes/ without route_class=ExecutionAPIRoute.
clusters.rationale: Without it allowed_token_types silently falls back to {"execution"} only, so any future token:workload route on that router is blocked with no obvious cause.

clusters.rule: An execution-API parameter that widens a state mutation beyond the single task instance identified by the JWT subject (e.g. ?all_map_indices=true) must use a broader scope such as ti:fleet, require a leader check (map_index in (-1, 0)), or document the intentional fleet-wide authority in the docstring.
clusters.trigger: An endpoint gains a parameter (e.g. all_map_indices: bool) that lets one task instance's token mutate sibling mapped task instances.
clusters.rationale: The execution token authorises one TI; silently letting it act on its siblings breaks the assumption the whole token scheme rests on.

clusters.rule: Execution-API list endpoints that query the metadata database must apply pagination (limit/offset) or a documented hard cap.
clusters.trigger: A GET list route in the execution API calls session.scalars(stmt).all() with no limit or offset.
clusters.rationale: Tables like Variables are unbounded in real deployments, so an unbounded list query is a slow query on the metadata database that every worker can trigger.

clusters.rule: Use log.debug rather than log.info for fall-through diagnostics on high-volume execution-API paths such as heartbeat.
clusters.trigger: log.info(...) is added on a fallback or miss path inside a heartbeat or other high-frequency execution API handler.
clusters.rationale: These handlers run per task instance per heartbeat interval; INFO there floods production logs and hides everything else.

clusters.rule: When archiving a task_instance_history row on the retry path, copy rendered_map_index whenever the field is present in the patch payload, including when its value is None.
clusters.trigger: A TIH archive path sets ti._rendered_map_index only under `if ti_patch_payload.rendered_map_index is not None:`.
clusters.rationale: The None check conflates "field absent" with "field cleared", so a deliberately cleared value never reaches the archived row.

clusters.rule: Declare static-path routes (e.g. HEAD routes) before parameterised routes at the same prefix in the execution API so greedy path-parameter matching cannot swallow them.
clusters.trigger: @router.head(...) declarations are reordered or removed relative to @router.get(...) with overlapping path patterns in the execution API routes.
clusters.rationale: FastAPI matches in declaration order, so a parameterised route declared first captures requests meant for the static one.

clusters.rule: config.yml descriptions must not name internal database tables; describe the concept in user-facing terms instead.
clusters.trigger: A description: in config.yml references an internal table name such as "task_state rows" or "dag_run rows".
clusters.rationale: These descriptions are rendered as operator-facing documentation, and the schema they name is not a public contract.

clusters.rule: Extract logic shared between sibling asset-store endpoints (e.g. /by-uri/value and /by-name/value) into a helper instead of duplicating the body after the resolve call.
clusters.trigger: A second execution-API asset-store route repeats the body of an existing route after its _resolve_asset_id_by_* call.
clusters.rationale: The reviewer flagged the copied body as guaranteed to drift between the two routes.

clusters.rule: Do not add email- or SMTP-related configuration options to airflow-core; route email settings through the SMTP provider.
clusters.trigger: A new config key referencing email, SMTP, or a notifier default is added to airflow-core/src/airflow/config_templates/config.yml.
clusters.rationale: Email delivery moved out of core into the provider; core options for it recreate the coupling that migration removed.

clusters.rule: Do not define domain-model enums (e.g. WeightRule) in configuration.py; put them in the module that owns the concept.
clusters.trigger: A class definition for an Enum or domain type is added to airflow-core/src/airflow/configuration.py.
clusters.rationale: configuration.py is imported extremely early and by everything; putting domain types there creates import cycles and makes the concept unfindable.

clusters.rule: Expose internal collections from AirflowConfigParser through methods returning immutable sequences (tuple), not as mutable list properties.
clusters.trigger: A @property in AirflowConfigParser or a subclass is annotated as returning list[...].
clusters.rationale: A returned list lets a caller mutate parser state in place, and the config parser is global.

clusters.rule: Type warning_types-style parameters as an open-ended homogeneous tuple (tuple[DagWarningType, ...]) rather than a fixed-length tuple.
clusters.trigger: A parameter typed tuple[DagWarningType, DagWarningType] is added or modified in dag_processing/collection.py.
clusters.rationale: A fixed-length tuple type breaks every caller the moment another warning type is added.

clusters.rule: In DagBundleManager._refresh_dag_bundles, remove a bundle from _force_refresh_bundles only after DB persistence succeeds, and clear _bundle_versions when persistence fails.
clusters.trigger: A bundle is removed from _force_refresh_bundles before update_bundle_state, or an exception from update_bundle_state is swallowed without clearing _bundle_versions.
clusters.rationale: The reviewer traced a case where a failed persist left a stale version cached and short-circuited the next refresh.

clusters.rule: Do not rely on a SQLAlchemy UPDATE returning rowcount == 0 to detect a missing row; use an explicit SELECT or EXISTS check.
clusters.trigger: `if result.rowcount == 0: raise` follows a single-row update() call.
clusters.rationale: rowcount semantics differ across the databases Airflow supports, including returning 0 for an update that matched but changed nothing.

clusters.rule: Docstrings on overridable DAG-processing methods must state the conditions under which the default implementation does nothing.
clusters.trigger: A method in dag_processing/ intended for override has a docstring that omits its no-op conditions.
clusters.rationale: Subclass authors outside the repo cannot see the body, and a silently skipped default is indistinguishable from a broken override.

clusters.rule: In DagFileProcessorProcess, pass dag_file.rel_path from the DagFileInfo object instead of recomputing it with Path.relative_to().
clusters.trigger: dag_processing/processor.py calls Path(path).relative_to(bundle_path) when a DagFileInfo with rel_path is already in the call chain.
clusters.rationale: The reviewer pointed at the value already carried through the call chain.

clusters.rule: A fix to an example DAG for a timezone or datetime bug must come with a regression test that imports the DAG under a non-UTC [core] default_timezone.
clusters.trigger: An example_dags/ file is modified to fix a datetime/timezone issue with no test exercising a non-UTC default_timezone.
clusters.rationale: These bugs only appear when the configured timezone is not UTC, which is exactly what the default test environment never exercises.

clusters.rule: Guard setproctitle usage in executor entry-points (BaseExecutor.run_workload and friends) with a darwin platform check.
clusters.trigger: Code under airflow-core/src/airflow/executors/ calls setproctitle() without a `sys.platform != "darwin"` or equivalent guard.
clusters.rationale: setproctitle misbehaves on macOS, which is where a large share of contributors run the executors locally.

clusters.rule: Generate the executor workload type error message from the ExecutorWorkload union rather than listing the type names by hand in an f-string.
clusters.trigger: An f-string in base_executor.py enumerates concrete workload type names manually instead of unpacking the type alias.
clusters.rationale: The reviewer noted the hand-written list would go stale the next time a workload type was added.

clusters.rule: In prepare_file_queue, look file stats up through the pre-built presence_key index dict in O(1) rather than scanning _file_stats linearly per file.
clusters.trigger: dag_processing/manager.py builds a dict keyed by file.presence_key but then calls a helper (e.g. processed_recently) that iterates over _file_stats.
clusters.rationale: The linear helper inside the per-file loop makes queue preparation O(n squared) in the number of DAG files, which large deployments feel directly.

clusters.rule: After queuing a workload with an executor, set the workload state to QUEUED, not RUNNING.
clusters.trigger: callback.state (or an equivalent workload state) is set to RUNNING immediately after executor.queue_workload().
clusters.rationale: Queueing is not acceptance; marking it running means a workload the executor never picked up looks in-flight forever.

clusters.rule: Do not add a separate query for an individual task state inside the scheduler critical section; fold the new state condition into the existing query.
clusters.trigger: A new session.execute(select(...).where(TI.state == ...)) is added inside _critical_section_* or an adjacent scheduler method.
clusters.rationale: The critical section holds locks other schedulers wait on, so each additional round trip lengthens the window for every scheduler in the deployment.

clusters.rule: Any new scheduler workload type must check available executor slots before submitting, following _enqueue_executor_callbacks and _critical_section_enqueue_task_instances.
clusters.trigger: A new method calls executor.queue_workload() for a new workload type without first reading available executor slots.
clusters.rationale: Ignoring slots lets one workload type starve task instances of the executor's fixed capacity.

clusters.rule: Select scheduler-owned rows that concurrent schedulers could pick up with with_row_locks(..., skip_locked=True).
clusters.trigger: session.scalars(select(<Model>).where(...)) inside the scheduler loop returns rows that are then mutated or dispatched, with no with_row_locks wrapper.
clusters.rationale: Airflow supports multiple active schedulers; without skip-locked selection two of them dispatch the same row.

clusters.rule: Prefer a ~exists(select(...).where(...)) anti-join over <col>.not_in(select(...)) in ORM queries.
clusters.trigger: The diff contains .not_in(select(...)) or NOT IN (SELECT ...) in a SQLAlchemy query.
clusters.rationale: NOT IN against a subquery that can yield NULL returns no rows at all, and it prevents the planner from using an index.

clusters.rule: A foreign-key column used as a subquery filter predicate in scheduler queries must have an explicit Index(...) declaration unless an existing index is confirmed to cover it.
clusters.trigger: A subquery filter on an FK column (e.g. .where(<Model>.trigger_id == ...)) is added with no Index("idx_<table>_<column>", ...) in the model definition.
clusters.rationale: Airflow does not get an index on an FK for free on all supported databases, and these predicates run on every scheduler loop.

clusters.rule: To call get_template_context from the triggerer, construct a RuntimeTaskInstance via RuntimeTaskInstance.model_construct(...); do not call it on a plain TaskInstance.

clusters.rule: Paginated bulk-action API endpoints must have a test that exercises multi-page traversal (e.g. `limit=1`) to prove the action applies across every page.
clusters.trigger: diff adds tests for a paginated bulk PATCH/POST endpoint with no `limit=1` case.
clusters.rationale: Bulk handlers commonly act only on the first page; single-page tests never see it.

clusters.rule: New task-group / task-instance state-change API handlers must have unmocked integration tests covering upstream and downstream propagation, past/future run coverage and the deadlock/409 paths.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a `TestPatch*TaskGroup`/`TestPatch*TaskInstance` class whose tests all mock the underlying state-transition method.
clusters.rationale: Mocking the transition leaves the real DB logic — the part that breaks — untested.

clusters.rule: Tests for endpoint parameters that accept several values (e.g. True/False/None filter flags) must be `@pytest.mark.parametrize`d, not folded into one assertion block.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a test function asserting several filter-param combinations sequentially in a single body.
clusters.rationale: Parametrized cases report which combination failed instead of stopping at the first assertion.

clusters.rule: Tests for async-generator middleware in the execution API (e.g. `_extract_w3c_trace_context`) must cover the `athrow` path and assert whether `detach` is called on it.
clusters.trigger: diff adds or modifies tests for such a generator without a case that throws into the generator.
clusters.rationale: Route errors take the throw path, which is where context leaks happen.

clusters.rule: When an execution-API feature claims multi-backend support through SQLAlchemy constructs such as `regexp_match`, its tests must run against every claimed backend, not just Postgres.
clusters.trigger: diff adds tests marked only `@pytest.mark.backend("postgres")` for a backend-portable construct.
clusters.rationale: These constructs compile differently per dialect, so a Postgres-only test proves nothing about MySQL or SQLite.

clusters.rule: Version-compat guards in airflow-core tests must name the lowest Airflow version at which the change actually landed (e.g. `AIRFLOW_V_3_0_PLUS` when the move happened in 3.0).
clusters.trigger: diff uses `AIRFLOW_V_3_1_PLUS` or higher to guard a symbol introduced or moved in an earlier 3.x release.
clusters.rationale: An over-tight guard silently skips the test on versions where it should run.

clusters.rule: Guard performance-motivated ORM changes (e.g. replacing `session.merge()` with `session.add()`) with an `assert_queries_count()` assertion so a regression fails CI.
clusters.trigger: diff swaps `session.merge(` for `session.add(` on a `task_instance`/`dag_run` path with no accompanying `assert_queries_count`.
clusters.rationale: Without a query-count assertion the win silently disappears on the next refactor.

clusters.rule: Bugfix entries in `chart/RELEASE_NOTES.rst` must be a concise one-line title; the detailed explanation belongs in the PR, not the release note.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a multi-sentence bugfix entry to `chart/RELEASE_NOTES.rst`.
clusters.rationale: Release notes are scanned as a list; long entries break the format.

clusters.rule: When a Helm value is split into executor-specific keys (e.g. `workers.labels` into `workers.celery.labels` / `workers.kubernetes.labels`), document it as deprecated in favour of the per-executor keys — with an example for each new key — and never as a 'rename'.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a deprecation notice in chart docs, `NOTES.txt` or `_helpers.yaml` that says 'renamed to X' for a split value, or removes the worker example without adding one per new key.
clusters.rationale: There is no single replacement key; calling it a rename tells users to migrate to the wrong one.

clusters.rule: `chart/newsfragments/*.significant.rst` entries for breaking changes must enumerate every removed Helm value with its replacement as an explicit old-to-new mapping, not a prose summary.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a `.significant.rst` newsfragment mentioning removed values or dropped executor support without listing the specific key mappings.
clusters.rationale: Users upgrade by diffing their values file against this list; prose leaves them guessing.

clusters.rule: Kustomize-overlay CI must not pull arbitrary third-party DockerHub images without an image-allowlist validation step.
clusters.trigger: diff adds an `image:` referencing a third-party DockerHub image under `chart/kustomize-overlays/` with no allowlist or validation check.
clusters.rationale: An untrusted image running in CI can exfiltrate the job's credentials.

clusters.rule: The Helm OTel collector ConfigMap must expose a values key that lets users supply their own complete collector `config.yml` instead of only the Airflow-generated body.
clusters.trigger: diff adds an OTel collector ConfigMap template with no `.Values` override for the whole config body.
clusters.rationale: Collector configs are highly site-specific; without a full override users must fork the chart.

clusters.trigger: diff renders both `traces:` and `metrics:` pipelines unconditionally regardless of which backends are enabled.
clusters.rationale: An unconditional pipeline makes the collector fail or export to a backend the user never configured.

clusters.rule: In Helm Service templates, name the user-supplied annotations key `.Values.<component>.service.annotations` (not `extraAnnotations`) when the resource has no Airflow-generated annotations of its own.
clusters.trigger: diff introduces `.Values.<component>.service.extraAnnotations` on a Service where no Airflow-generated annotations are applied.
clusters.rationale: `extra` only makes sense when it is added to something; otherwise the key just reads wrong.

clusters.rule: Tests for `@operator_defaults` must include a case where the operator explicitly overrides the decorator's default (e.g. `retries=0` beating `@operator_defaults(retries=3)`).
clusters.trigger: diff adds `@operator_defaults` test cases that only cover the decorator supplying its value.
