clusters.rule: DAG serialization test fixtures containing fields that are always emitted because their defaults come from `airflow.cfg` at parse time (e.g. `catchup`, `max_active_runs`, `max_active_tasks`) must carry an inline comment saying so.
clusters.trigger: diff adds or edits a serialization fixture including such fields with no explanatory comment.
clusters.rationale: They look redundant against the schema, and future readers delete them.

clusters.rule: Sentinel objects such as `NOTSET` and `SET_DURING_EXECUTION` must have `repr()` and `str()` return the same stable string their `serialize()` produces, not the class name.
clusters.trigger: diff changes `__repr__`/`__str__` on a sentinel class to return the class name.
clusters.rationale: The serialized form is what shows up in logs and stored payloads; two spellings of the same sentinel confuse comparisons.

clusters.rule: A test that takes the `caplog` fixture must assert on captured log output; if there is nothing to assert, remove `caplog` and its setup.
clusters.trigger: A test function accepts `caplog` but contains no assertion against `caplog.text` or `caplog.records`.
clusters.rationale: Unused caplog implies coverage that is not there and slows the test.

clusters.rule: Do not bundle unrelated tightening (e.g. adding `spec=` to an existing MagicMock) into a PR whose title describes a distinct bug fix; drop the hunk or call it out in the PR body.
clusters.trigger: diff modifies an existing `mock.MagicMock()` to add `spec=` in a file otherwise changed only for an unrelated fix.
clusters.rationale: Unannounced extra changes make the fix harder to review and to revert.

clusters.rule: In `topological_sort` and other task-group ordering paths, index positions with a `dict[task_id, index]` rather than repeated `list.index()` lookups.
clusters.trigger: diff introduces or retains a `.index(` call on a list inside a topological-sort or task-group ordering function.
clusters.rationale: `.index()` in the loop makes ordering O(n squared) on DAGs with many tasks.

clusters.rule: Docker Compose services under `airflow-e2e-tests/` must not set a fixed `container_name`, must address each other by service-name hostname, and must not publish host ports without a demonstrated external need.
clusters.trigger: diff adds `container_name:` or a host-port mapping to a service in a compose file under `airflow-e2e-tests/`.
clusters.rationale: Fixed names and published ports collide with whatever else is running on the CI host or a developer's machine.

clusters.rule: In `chart/RELEASE_NOTES.rst`, wrap every Helm values key reference in double RST backticks (e.g. ``workers.celery.nodeSelector``).
clusters.trigger: diff adds a line to `chart/RELEASE_NOTES.rst` containing a dotted Helm values path without surrounding double backticks.
clusters.rationale: Unmarked paths render as prose and are unreadable in the published notes.

clusters.rule: In `chart/values.yaml`, describe auto-generated config values as 'generated by default from `.Values.<helmPath>`' and point users at the Helm value, rather than calling the config key deprecated or the override the only option.
clusters.trigger: A values.yaml comment says a config key is 'deprecated' or 'only possible' via direct `config.*` override when the chart actually generates it from a Helm value.
clusters.rationale: The comment steers users away from the supported knob toward a raw override.

clusters.rule: When a Helm config flag's behaviour depends on another value (e.g. `statsd_on` gated on `otelCollector.metricsEnabled`), document the dependency in both `values.yaml` and `values.schema.json`.
clusters.trigger: A conditional expression in the `config:` block of values.yaml references two or more `.Values` fields but only one carries an explanatory comment.
clusters.rationale: Users setting one flag cannot discover that another silently overrides it.

clusters.rule: CI reproduction instructions generated by Breeze must check out `GITHUB_SHA`, not `FETCH_HEAD`, so the instructions keep pointing at the commit that failed.
clusters.trigger: A `ReproductionCommand` in `reproduce_ci.py` emits `git checkout FETCH_HEAD` after fetching `refs/pull/...`.
clusters.rationale: `FETCH_HEAD` moves as the PR advances, so the reproduction no longer reproduces.

clusters.rule: When Breeze renders CLI flags into reproduction commands, emit the long-form alias (`param.opts[-1]` / `param.secondary_opts[-1]`), not the first alias.
clusters.trigger: A flag-pair branch in `build_reproduction_command_from_context()` uses `param.opts[0]` or `param.secondary_opts[0]`.
clusters.rationale: The first alias may be a single-letter short flag, which is unreadable in a pasted reproduction command.

clusters.rule: The `KUSTOMIZE_OVERLAYS_FILES` group in `selective_checks.py` must include `^chart/templates/` and `^chart/files/`.
clusters.trigger: diff adds or edits `FileGroupForCi.KUSTOMIZE_OVERLAYS_FILES` without those patterns.
clusters.rationale: Overlay smoke tests render Helm templates, so template-only changes must trigger them.

clusters.rule: Breeze utility functions must not mix human-readable error sentinel strings into a `list[str]` of job names; signal lookup failure with `None`, a result object, or an exception.
clusters.trigger: A function returning `list[str]` (or a similar job-name collection) returns a string constant such as `FAILED_JOBS_LOOKUP_ERROR` on failure.
clusters.rationale: Callers cannot distinguish a job named like the sentinel from a failure, and the type says nothing about it.

clusters.rule: Tests for Breeze CLI flag-pair rendering must include a flag that has both a short and a long alias, asserting the long form is the one emitted.
clusters.trigger: A test in `dev/breeze/tests/` for flag-rendering logic only covers flags with a single long form.
clusters.rationale: The alias-selection bug only shows up when there is more than one alias to choose from.

clusters.rule: Do not put implementation-detail comments in `chart/values.yaml`; comments there describe what the field controls, not template guard logic, schema mechanics or helper internals.
clusters.trigger: A values.yaml comment explains internal template or Helm helper behaviour rather than the field's user-facing effect.
clusters.rationale: values.yaml is user documentation; internal notes belong in the templates.

clusters.rule: Release-tooling shell scripts under `dev/` must branch on `$(uname)` so both macOS (BSD `date`) and Linux (GNU `date`) syntax work.
clusters.trigger: A shell script in `dev/` uses GNU-only `date --utc` or BSD-only `date -v` with no OS check.
clusters.rationale: Release managers run these scripts on both platforms.

clusters.rule: Images used only by kustomize-overlay smoke tests must not be added to the static Breeze k8s image preload list; they are discovered from the overlay manifest by `_discover_overlay_images()`.
clusters.trigger: A new image entry is added to the static k8s preload list in `kubernetes_commands.py` for an image that appears only under `chart/kustomize-overlays/`.
clusters.rationale: Duplicating the entry means the two lists drift and every overlay change needs a Breeze edit.

clusters.rule: New path-parsing or git-worktree logic in Breeze must be covered by unit tests for an absolute gitdir path, a relative gitdir path, and the non-worktree case.
clusters.trigger: A function reading `.git` file content or deriving paths from `AIRFLOW_ROOT_PATH` is added to `path_utils.py`/`shell_params.py` without those three cases.
clusters.rationale: Worktree layouts vary by git version and by how the worktree was created; only all three cases prove the parsing.

clusters.rule: Fragile path-derivation logic in Breeze (e.g. locating the main `.git` directory from a worktree gitdir) must live in one helper; do not duplicate it across `docker_command_utils.py` and `shell_params.py`.
clusters.trigger: A `.parent.parent`-style worktree-root derivation appears in more than one file under `dev/breeze/src/`.
clusters.rationale: Two copies of a fragile heuristic fall out of sync the first time git changes its layout.

clusters.rule: `get_git_worktree_root()` must resolve a relative `gitdir:` path to an absolute path (against `AIRFLOW_ROOT_PATH`) before returning it.
clusters.trigger: `Path(git_content.removeprefix("gitdir: "))` is returned without an `is_absolute()` check and resolution.
clusters.rationale: Docker bind mounts require absolute paths, so a relative gitdir breaks the container mount.

clusters.rule: When invoking or documenting `prek` in Breeze code and messages, use `--hook-stage`, not `--stage`.
clusters.trigger: A prek invocation or instructional string under `dev/breeze/` uses `--stage`.
clusters.rationale: `--stage` is the pre-commit spelling; prek rejects it, so the printed instructions do not work.

clusters.rule: Breeze `CacheStore` entries must nest the stored payload under a dedicated key (e.g. `{"profile": ...}`) so cache metadata such as `cached_at` never leaks into the runtime object returned to callers.
clusters.trigger: A `CacheStore.save()` stores a plain dict and the matching `get()` result is used directly as the runtime object.
clusters.rationale: Callers then see cache bookkeeping fields as if they were real data.

clusters.rule: In a Trigger's polling loop, evaluate the execution deadline before checking job state, so a terminal status observed after the deadline still yields `timeout` rather than `success`/`error`.
clusters.trigger: diff adds or modifies a `while` loop in a Trigger `run()` that checks `is_still_running()` before comparing against `end_time`/`execution_deadline`.
clusters.rationale: Otherwise the timeout is silently overridden by whatever status the last poll happened to see.

clusters.rule: Helm test coverage for deprecated-but-still-supported value overrides (e.g. `workers.keda.query`) must be kept when the executor or CRD that exercised them is removed; migrate the case to an equivalent supported executor instead of deleting it.
clusters.trigger: diff deletes a helm test parametrize case covering a value path still listed in the `NOTES.txt` deprecation notice.
clusters.rationale: The value is still documented as working, so it still needs a test proving it does.

clusters.rule: Name Helm test helper variables after the Kubernetes workload they actually read; do not call a value read from the worker StatefulSet `broker_url_secret_in_scheduler`.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a helm test variable whose name references one workload while the value is fetched from another.
clusters.rationale: The mismatched name makes the assertion look like it covers a workload it never touches.

clusters.rule: Helm tests for a given component must live in that component's established `test_<component>.py` file, not be spread across other files.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a test class for a component (e.g. `TestMetadataConnectionTplRendering`) to a file other than the component's dedicated test file.
clusters.rationale: Scattered coverage means the next contributor cannot tell whether a case already exists.

clusters.rule: Version strings that must track an external release (e.g. the provider version pinned in the Edge Worker) must be declared as named constants at the top of the file or in a constants file, not embedded as literals inside functions.
clusters.trigger: diff changes a hard-coded version string literal inside a function or constructor in go-sdk or edge worker code.
clusters.rationale: A literal buried in a call site is missed at every release bump.

clusters.rule: Where the Go SDK and the Python supervisor use different frame-size caps for the IPC channel, each side's constant must carry a doc comment explaining its value and why the two sides differ.
clusters.trigger: diff adds or changes a frame/buffer-size constant in `go-sdk/pkg/execution/` with no comment relating it to the Python cap.
clusters.rationale: An unexplained asymmetry between the two ends of one protocol reads as a bug to the next reader.

clusters.rule: Go IPC message structs that use `-1` as a sentinel for `map_index` must document the convention in a comment, and should prefer a nullable `*int` to match the Python side's `int | None`.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a Go IPC struct with an `int` `MapIndex` field using -1 as a sentinel while the Python counterpart in `comms.py` uses `int | None`.
clusters.rationale: The two ends must agree on what 'no map index' means, or the sentinel is decoded as a real index.

clusters.rule: ADR documents must cite the actual function or method where the described behaviour lives; do not name a helper when the logic sits in the exported entry point.
clusters.trigger: diff adds or edits an ADR `.md` referencing a code symbol by name that does not match the real location.
clusters.rationale: ADRs are read as a map of the code; a wrong symbol sends readers to the wrong place.

clusters.rule: Source release tarballs built from the Java SDK must `export-ignore` binary wrapper artifacts such as `gradle-wrapper.jar`.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a `git archive` invocation in a Gradle release task without a `.gitattributes` export-ignore for `gradle-wrapper.jar`.
clusters.rationale: Binaries in the source release trip the Apache release checker during the RC vote.

clusters.rule: Public interfaces and classes in the Java/Kotlin SDK must carry KDoc/JavaDoc.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a `public interface` or `public class` under `java-sdk/sdk/src/main/kotlin/` with no KDoc block.
clusters.rationale: SDK documentation is generated from source and IDE users rely on the inline help.

clusters.rule: `execute_complete` must branch on `event["status"]` and handle every status its paired Trigger can emit — raising for error, cancelled and timeout statuses — before reading any payload field as a success.
clusters.trigger: diff implements or edits `execute_complete` that reads payload fields without a prior status check, or a Trigger gains a status (e.g. `"cancelled"`) with no matching branch in the operator.
clusters.rationale: A missing branch silently reports the task successful for a job that was cancelled or failed.

clusters.rule: Do not add a `stream()` stub that raises `NotImplementedError` to a log handler; leave the method absent so the framework's `getattr` check falls back to `read()`.
clusters.trigger: diff adds `def stream(self, ...): raise NotImplementedError` to a class inheriting from a remote log handler.
clusters.rationale: The log framework detects streaming support by attribute presence, so the stub turns a working fallback into a hard error.

clusters.rule: A provider's `tags` in `provider.yaml` must match the tags declared in its `get_provider_info.py`.
clusters.trigger: diff changes `tags:` in `provider.yaml` or the tags list in `get_provider_info.py` so the two disagree.
clusters.rationale: The two sources feed generated provider docs and produce conflicting categorisation.

clusters.rule: Hooks accepting an enum-like parameter such as `access_type` must validate it against the module's `VALID_*` constants and raise `ValueError` listing the allowed values before making any API call.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a hook method branching on `access_type`/`auth_type` with no `if ... not in VALID_...` guard first.
clusters.rationale: Without the guard a typo silently falls through to a default branch or a confusing remote error.

clusters.rule: Provider `changelog.rst` entries must use sentence-case commit titles; lowercase openers and conventional-commit prefixes such as `fix:` are not acceptable.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a line to `providers/*/docs/changelog.rst` whose title starts with a lowercase word or a `fix:`/`feat:` prefix.
clusters.rationale: The changelog is published prose, not a raw commit log.

clusters.rule: When tightening a provider dependency with a `<X.Y` upper bound, record — in a comment or a linked issue — the condition under which the cap can be lifted.
clusters.trigger: diff adds an upper-bound pin to a provider dependency without an accompanying note explaining when it may be relaxed.
clusters.rationale: Undocumented caps outlive the incompatibility that caused them and block users for releases on end.

clusters.rule: A Trigger test that verifies one deadline path (e.g. `execution_deadline`) must set the other deadline (`end_time`) to a future value so exactly one timeout branch is exercised.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a Trigger unit test where both `end_time` and `execution_deadline` are already expired.
clusters.rationale: With both expired the test passes whichever branch fires and proves neither.

clusters.rule: When refactoring an operator's execution paths, a documented parameter (e.g. `awslogs_enabled`) must keep its documented effect in both the deferrable and non-deferrable paths.
clusters.trigger: diff refactors deferrable execution and leaves a previously-honoured parameter with no effect in `execute_complete`.
clusters.rationale: The parameter is still documented and still set by users; silently ignoring it in one path is a behaviour regression.

clusters.rule: Operator links whose data only exists after the job completes (e.g. a CloudWatch log stream ARN) must be persisted after the wait, not before it, in the non-deferrable path.
clusters.trigger: diff calls `_persist_links()` or equivalent before `hook.wait_for_job()` where the link data is only available post-completion.
clusters.rationale: Persisting early stores an incomplete link that never resolves for the user.

clusters.rule: When changing behaviour that existing tests cover, update the tests to cover both the new branch and the altered or removed one; do not leave assertions describing behaviour that no longer exists.
clusters.trigger: diff changes conditional logic in an operator without adding or updating tests for both sides of the condition.
clusters.rationale: Stale assertions pass while describing the wrong contract.

clusters.rule: Amazon provider docstrings must append `(templated)` to the description of every parameter listed in `template_fields`.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a `:param:` line in an Amazon provider operator, trigger or sensor for a field present in `template_fields` without the `(templated)` marker.
clusters.rationale: Users cannot otherwise tell which arguments accept Jinja.

clusters.rule: An AWS operator's `execute()` should return a minimal meaningful identifier (ARN, URI, name) rather than the raw boto3 response dict.
clusters.trigger: diff ends an AWS operator's `execute()` with `return response` where `response` is the raw boto3 response.
clusters.rationale: The whole response becomes an XCom payload with metadata users neither need nor can rely on.

clusters.rule: Provider how-to RST docs must order lifecycle sections to follow the resource lifecycle: Create, Start, Stop, Update, Delete.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a section to a provider how-to doc out of lifecycle order.
clusters.rationale: Readers follow these pages top to bottom as a walkthrough.

clusters.rule: A constraint stated in an operator docstring (e.g. a maximum list size) must be enforced by a runtime check in `__init__`; do not document bounds that are not validated.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a docstring stating a numeric bound for a parameter with no matching validation in `__init__`.
clusters.rationale: An unvalidated bound surfaces as an opaque API error at execution time instead of a clear failure at parse time.

clusters.rule: In `BaseExecutor._process_workloads` and its overrides, name the sequence parameter `workload_items`, not `workloads`.
clusters.trigger: diff adds or edits an executor method with a parameter named `workloads` in a module that also does `from airflow.executors import workloads`.
clusters.rationale: The parameter otherwise shadows the imported module inside the method body.

clusters.rule: AWS executors must not log each individual task failure inline; aggregate failures and log them once at the summary point.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a `self.log.info(...)`/`self.log.error(...)` inside a per-task failure branch of an AWS executor sync loop.
clusters.rationale: A large failing batch floods the scheduler log with one line per task.

clusters.rule: AWS hooks that build a boto3 client must subclass the Boto-specific base (`AwsBaseHook`), not the generic `BaseHook`.
clusters.trigger: diff adds an AWS hook importing `BaseHook` from `airflow.providers.common.compat.sdk` while creating a boto3 client itself.
clusters.rationale: `AwsBaseHook` already handles session, region and credential resolution consistently with every other AWS hook.

clusters.rule: In `execute_complete`, read all required state from the trigger event dict; never fall back to an attribute set during `execute`.
clusters.trigger: diff uses `self.job_id` or another `execute`-time attribute inside `execute_complete` as a fallback when the event lacks the value.
clusters.rationale: `execute_complete` runs in a fresh task instance after deferral, so those attributes are not the ones `execute` set.

clusters.rule: Do not replace `AirflowException` with `RuntimeError` in operator, sensor or trigger error paths without auditing every caller that catches the original type.
clusters.trigger: diff removes `raise AirflowException(` and adds `raise RuntimeError(` in an operator, sensor or trigger.
clusters.rationale: Downstream code and user DAGs catch the declared type; swapping it silently changes which handlers fire.

clusters.rule: Avoid adding unit tests that only re-exercise paths an existing broader test already covers; prefer fewer, higher-value tests over branch-by-branch duplication.
clusters.trigger: diff adds several small test functions each covering a single branch already exercised as a sub-case of an existing test in the same file.
clusters.rationale: Duplicate coverage costs CI time and has to be maintained twice.

clusters.rule: In caplog-based trigger tests, call `caplog.set_level(...)` before invoking the method under test.

clusters.rationale: Otherwise capture depends on the ambient log level and the test fails only on some machines.

clusters.rule: Use the provider's existing Hook class (e.g. `KafkaProducerHook`) rather than constructing the underlying client directly inside operator, trigger or listener code.
clusters.trigger: diff constructs a provider client (e.g. `confluent_kafka.Producer(...)`) directly where a Hook already wraps it.
clusters.rationale: The hook is where connection resolution, extras handling and lifecycle already live.

clusters.rule: Instance attributes — resource handles such as a consumer or client, and state flags such as submission status — must be initialised in `__init__` and, for resources, reset to `None` after cleanup; do not first-assign or reset them inside `run()`, `submit()` or `execute()`.

clusters.rationale: Attributes that only exist after a method runs make cleanup non-idempotent and raise `AttributeError` on the paths that never ran it.

clusters.rule: Operator parameters referenced as `self.<param>` in `execute()`/`execute_complete()` must be declared as constructor arguments and assigned in `__init__`.
clusters.trigger: diff references `self.<param>` in an operator method where `<param>` is absent from the class `__init__` signature.
clusters.rationale: Users cannot set the value and the attribute does not exist at runtime.

clusters.rule: In `SparkSubmitHook.submit()`, post-submit commands and cleanup that must run after the job finishes belong in a `try/finally` so they execute whether the job succeeded or raised.
